c7.declared_deviation: the engine uses the SI-defined constants, not the declared ten-digit doubles. The deviation reaches one compared row, this one. Of the abs rows whose band is below 1e-9 of their reference, the others are integer cycle counts that the constants do not enter (D332's sweep), and R/F's 1.6e-11 moves a 0.1 V root by about 2e-12 V, far inside every voltage band
c7.ruling: proposed for the lead's ruling, which the lead's tag of this erratum makes: the row's relative tolerance is floored at 1e-10. The stored 1e-12 is the references' proposed tolerance (tol_source: 'DESIGN C7: charge 1e-9 C; relative 1e-12 proposed'), which REFERENCES_USAGE.md leaves open to the lead's ruling by a dated note; this erratum, once tagged, is that note. The judge first checks the stored band against the band rule, as for every abs row. It then compares with max(that band, max(tol_abs + 1e-10 |reference|, 10 floor)), and records both bands
c7.why_1e-10: a property of the declared input, not of the observed gap. The declared F is stated to ten significant digits, so half a unit in its last digit is 5.2e-11 relative, and any F that rounds to the declared value lies within that of the reference's. 1e-10 is the smallest power of ten above it, and it is not tighter than the two sides' constants agree (3.43e-11). The row then tests the pump's net charge per cycle, not which F an implementation holds. At 1e-12 no implementation of the SI constants could pass it
c7.not_chosen: declaring the SI constants instead would change a declared input after an engine output. The references would then recompute this row, and every F- and R-dependent row for one F on their side: a references amendment and a second values file. Here no declared constant changes, so the references are not recomputed and no request goes to their owner
c7.known_when_ruled: proposed knowing D329's gap (3.43e-11 relative) and D332's cause. The prior property that fixes the value is the declared F's ten digits

c8b.horizon_reason: set by the slowest mode of the bare node and face, the electroneutral K+/Na+ exchange: tau_slow 9.36 s (the declared log-mean face law linearised at the Donnan state, D332; the engine's own late rate gives 9.35 s), not DESIGN's single-ion 7.5 s on which erratum 1's horizon was set. 192 s is 20.5 tau_slow, over which the slow mode falls by exp(-20.5) = 1.2e-9. Even K's whole initial distance (4 mM to its end value, 4.2 times that value) in the slow mode would leave 5e-9 relative, 0.005 of the registered 1e-6 band. Projected from D329's own 64 s residual (5.0e-4 in K, which the reference's own RK4 run shares), it leaves 6e-10. 192 s is the first multiple of 64 s (the coupled run's horizon and the reference's run length) past 20 tau_slow. The coupled run keeps 64 s: its rows read it at stated times, and its 1/e times (about 4.8 s) lie well inside

The ratio does not depend on B_out: version 1's J = k a S (1 - e^x), S > 0, vanishes where x = 0, and x holds B only as B_in/B_out (DESIGN §3.3). Erratum 1's 10 mM, the dose bath's B, put 1e6 to 1e10 fmol of B in the cell at the roots (D332)
c6.domain_reason: it contains every registered root, which reach 1.66e7 (D332); erratum 1's [1e-6, 1e6] left 4 keys' roots beyond it. The lower end is erratum 1's
c6.float64: every world of every scan holds each node's charge-anchor terms (its fixed background and its ionic sum) below 2^19 fmol, where the parse's absolute 1e-20 C check (surface_tissue.check_definition) cannot fail. The two roundings it meets reach at most 2^(k-52) fmol in the binade [2^k, 2^(k+1)), 5.6e-21 C below 2^19 fmol (D332). At B_out 1e-5 mM the scan's largest B_in is 1,000 mM, 65,450 fmol in the 65.45 pL cell. Over all 344 rows the largest term is 81,100 fmol (the held bath at Na 91 mM), 6.5 times below the bound (xc0_engine anchor-bound: arithmetic on the worlds' entries, nothing parsed). Each term is linear in B_in, so a scan's two ends bound it, and the reading checks them again before any world is parsed (xc0_engine.eq_ratio_e2)
c6.scan_refusal: a bracket scan counts the points it did not evaluate (refused at parse, outside a law's domain, not finite), and its refusal states them, so that 'no sign change' cannot hide a stretch never evaluated. procedure: 1. The lead tags this erratum's head. The runner checks that git rev-parse <tag>:src equals git rev-parse 260d7c7f:src (2c5a51cb47b2613dd9dd785541dd1d2ee0003379) and records both: the rerun's engine is 260d7c7f's (D333)

2. Freeze: the runner's own detached worktree of the tag, then scripts/gates/freeze_snapshot.py <worktree> <out> --scope full --require-clean. From the snapshot, xc0_compare.check_rule() passes. Every later step runs from it, with PYTHONPATH=<snapshot>/src:<snapshot> and JAX_ENABLE_X64=1

3. The rerun's manifest, names and keys only: xc0_compare check-keys KEYS (KEYS the keys stage's keys.json, rerun.keys; exit 0, the counts in coverage), then xc0_compare manifest KEYS MANIFEST --changed (352 rows of the six changed families; no calibrations, since T1 and T2 are D329's), then xc0_compare carry-check KEYS <rerun.base.judge_json> (exit 0: D329's judged rows are the interface's, each once)
4. The anchor bound: xc0_engine anchor-bound MANIFEST (arithmetic on the worlds' entries, no engine value): 344 rows, all below 2^19 fmol

5. The P1LB runs on a gate lane under its lock, one segment per core, as D329's: xc0_engine c8b-run READING FACTOR UNTIL RUNS/<reading>-<factor:g>/seg<N> --x2-cap 0.002 [--resume PREVIOUS]. The bare readings at factors 1 and 0.5 run in three segments each, ending at 64, 128 and 192 s, each resuming its predecessor. The coupled readings at 1 and 0.5 run to 64 s, one segment each. Batch 1 runs the four first segments; batches 2 and 3 run the bare readings' second and third. Each segment's record is checked against the snapshot (revision, empty patch, cap 0.002, trajectory digest, resume chain) before the table. Yield as D329's runs did (FR-43 first, then gates); never CPUs 12-15 or 28-31 or the timed cores 4, 5, 20 and 21

6. The table: xc0_engine table MANIFEST OUT --x2-cap 0.002 --c8b RUNS under scripts/run_detached.sh on CPU 6, 7, 22 or 23 (about 10 minutes: 344 static rows of about a second, 7 C8b rows from the saved runs). Its sha256 is recorded in the run folder before the judge runs

7. The judge: xc0_compare judge TABLE VALUES BANDS OUT --carry <rerun.base.judge_json>, VALUES and BANDS the snapshot's designs/ files. It checks check_rule, the table's clean snapshot and cap, the base snapshot's record digest and the same engine, and the carried file's digest. It then resolves every changed row with the values file unopened (a refusal prints names and keys only), judges the changed families, and carries D329's rows of the others

8. The retry, once, as tagged: xc0_compare retry-manifest TABLE RETRY_MANIFEST, then xc0_engine table RETRY_MANIFEST OUT2 --x2-cap 0.002 --retry --c8b RUNS, then xc0_compare judge TABLE VALUES BANDS OUT --retry OUT2/engine_table.json --carry <rerun.base.judge_json>. A C8b row's retry needs the P1LB runs at h/4 (c8b.cost); the runner asks the lead before them

9. The verdict record, in a new folder (D329's record untouched): overall, claim, family and row outcomes, which rows are carried and which rerun, the tables' and the carried file's digests, each C6 row's scan counts, each ion's relative change in the bare run from 160 s to 192 s beside C8.b_final_* (information), and not_blind (this erratum's and the runner's)
